findings: l.647 'By assumption, the quotient is Hausdorff': Hausdorffness of Gamma\M does not follow from the neighbourhood form of proper discontinuity alone (free wandering actions with non-Hausdorff quotients exist); it needs the separating form (IsProperlyDiscontinuous.separates, or local compactness with mathlib's definition). hypotheses.note: DEC-47 reading D = (z+σθ/α, r cos θ, r sin θ): GX.massive_particle_intended (formula on {r>0}, local homeomorphism, holonomy the screw motion of angle α and pitch σ, which is in Isom_0, unique quotient structure); mass read as 1 − angle/2π (literature convention)

hypotheses.paper: extreme BTZ black hole: D'(r,θ,t) = D(r,θ,−t)
hypotheses.note: DEC-47 reading: u past lightlike — GX.btz_blackhole_past_isom0 for every x0, every u with Q(u)=0, τ(u)<0, every v with <v|u> < 0, G = Isom_0: parabolic family P_θ ∈ Isom_0 fixing x0+Ru pointwise, D = P_θ(x0+rv+tu) a local homeomorphism on {r>0} with holonomy P_α, developing {r>0} into the past side <y−x0|−u> > 0 of the null plane through the singular line (the white hole develops into the future side, GX.btzDevGen_future_side; sign convention GX.nullB_neg_of_future), unique quotient structure

hypotheses.paper: variations: u spacelike, v spacelike or future/past timelike
hypotheses.note: DEC-52 corrected form: every x0, every spacelike u, every v with <v|w> != 0 for every nonzero null w orthogonal to u (GX.misner_variations_ruled, the hypothesis verbatim); timelike v satisfy it (GX.nullB_ne_zero_of_timelike, reverse Cauchy-Schwarz), spacelike v must be asked for it (GX.misnerDev_spacelike_counterexample)

DEC-52 corrected form sing(M) ⊆ π{r=0}, together with existence/uniqueness of the maximal a.e. structure and M ≅ ℂ × Z in one statement GX.quotientBase_ruled; the printed equality refuted by GX.quotientBase_counterexample

findings: l.667 'Its singular locus is sing(M) = {r=0}' is false in general: GX.quotientBase_counterexample (alpha = 2π, X = C, G = translations, D(r,θ) = r e^{iθ}, every hypothesis of the example) has EMPTY singular locus while {r=0} is the apex. True: sing(M) ⊆ π{r=0} (GX.quotientBase_sing_subset).

l.664–667 dimension slip: cyl{n} := D_inf × R^n is (n+2)-dimensional and is said to have a local homeomorphism {r>0} → X ⊆ R^n and a quotient homeomorphic to R^n; read cyl{n} = D_inf × R^{n-2} (the Minkowski case uses (r,θ,z), z ∈ R, X = R^3), or the quotient as R^{n+2}. Formalized for D_inf × Z, with M ≅ C × Z (GX.cylHomeomorph).

l.673 (massive particle), printed slip (DEC-47): with D(r,θ,z) = (z+σθ/α, r cos(θ/α), r sin(θ/α)) the deck generator θ ↦ θ+α of Γ_α acts by D ↦ (time translation by σ) ∘ (rotation of angle 1 radian), whatever α (GX.massiveDev_smul with c = 1/α). The cone angle is therefore 1 and the mass 1 − 1/2π, not m = 1 − α/2π, unless α = 1. The intended D = (z+σθ/α, r cos θ, r sin θ) (DEC-47) is GX.massive_particle_intended: angle α.

l.674–678 (extreme BTZ white hole): formalized in the paper's generality (GX.btz_whitehole_isom0: every x0, future lightlike u, <v|u> < 0, G = Isom_0); D is even a homeomorphism of {r>0} onto a half-space, holonomy P_α.

l.678, printed slip (DEC-47): 'Choosing D'(r,θ,t) = D(r,θ,−t) gives an extreme BTZ blackhole instead' — D' = D ∘ T with T(r,θ,t) = (r,θ,−t) a Γ_α-equivariant homeomorphism of the cylinder, so the printed black hole is isomorphic, as a singular (G,X)-manifold, to the white hole (GX.btz_blackhole_iso_whitehole, GX.btz_blackhole_isom0). The intended black hole takes u past lightlike (DEC-47): GX.btz_blackhole_past_isom0, which develops {r>0} into the past side of the null plane through the singular line, where the white hole develops into the future side (GX.btzDevGen_future_side).

l.679 (Misner/BTZ variations, u spacelike): 'v spacelike' does not suffice: for u = (0,0,1) and the spacelike v = (1,0,1) (null coordinates, Q(v) = 1) the image of D lies in a plane, so D is not a local homeomorphism (GX.misnerDev_spacelike_counterexample). Needed: v not in the plane spanned by u and one null eigendirection of the boosts (v_a v_b ≠ 0), automatic for timelike v. Formalized with that condition (GX.misner_btz, GX.misner_isom0).

l.679 (variations): the condition on v, stated intrinsically, is: ⟨v|w⟩ ≠ 0 for every nonzero null w ⊥ u (v off the two null planes spanned by u and a null eigenline of the boosts); automatic for timelike v (GX.misner_isom0_general, first disjunct), and 'v spacelike' alone allows a degenerate D (GX.misnerDev_spacelike_counterexample).

STATUS: closed under DEC-52 (sing(M) ⊆ π{r=0}; <v|w> != 0 for every nonzero null w ⊥ u) and DEC-47 (massive particle (r cos θ, r sin θ); past lightlike u for the black hole); the printed forms stay recorded as findings with their counterexamples. The dimension slip (cyl{n} = D_inf × R^n homeomorphic to R^n) is absorbed by the generality in Z (M ≅ ℂ × Z, GX.cylHomeomorph).

l.682 (tachyons, photons) and l.684 (polyhedral gluings) are informal remarks, not formalized (SCOPE (c)): no developing map, no element of PSL(2,R) nor which lift to the universal cover of RP^1 generates Γ (a lift fixing a lift of a fixed point acts on {r>0} with fixed points, the other lifts freely, so the choice decides freeness), 'tachyon'/'photon' undefined in the paper; no polyhedra or gluing maps given for l.684.

labels.label: ex:conical

hypotheses.note: 0 < α; R^{n-2} read as any locally connected T2 nonempty Z (a finite-dimensional Euclidean E for G = Isom+)

hypotheses.paper: metric dz^2+dr^2+α r^2 dθ^2, θ ∈ R/Z

proved, not read (round 1 fix): FundamentalGroup (π{r>0}) y₀ ≃* Multiplicative ℤ at every base point (GX.conical_fundamentalGroup, any α ≠ 0 via GX.fundamentalGroup_cylPos_int), by the isomorphism GX.fundamentalGroup_cylPos = UniversalCover.deckEquiv, transported through the homeomorphism Φ of previous_examples_universalCover (GX.deckCongrOfComp), then Deck ≃* Γ_1 (GX.cylPosDeck_bijective: injective by freeness on {r>0}, surjective by uniqueness of lifts on the connected — contractible — total space); χ conjugates each loop's deck transformation to the action of χ(g) ∈ Γ_1, so the holonomy ρ: π₁ = ℤ → G sends the generator to ρ_α (conicalDev_smul)

hypotheses.paper: holonomy ρ : π₁({r>0}) = ℤ → R^n ⋊ SO(n), ρ(1) the rotation of angle α, non-trivial when α ∉ 2πN*
hypotheses.note: one homomorphism ρ : π₁(π{r>0}, y₀) →* Isom⁺(𝔼^n) with the developing map ρ-equivariant, ρ = ρ_α^χ for χ : π₁ ≃* ℤ, ρ(1) = ρ_α, and ρ(1) = 1 in G iff α ∈ 2πN* (GX.conical_holonomy, GX.conicalRot_eq_one_iff)

findings: l.347, printed slip (DEC-47 reads angle α): with θ ∈ R/Z the metric dz²+dr²+α r² dθ² has cone angle √α (a circle r = r0 has length √α·r0), not α. Lean witness: read as the cone C_{√α}, its apex is Euclidean iff α = 4π² and NOT Euclidean at the paper's α = 2π (GX.conical_printed_metric, GX.conical_printed_metric_two_pi), against 'cannot be extended … except for α = 2π'. The rest of the example (holonomy = rotation of angle α) and ex:consider_identifying need angle α, i.e. α² r² dθ² on R/Z (or r² dθ² on R/αZ). The corrected object is built: E^n_α = C_α × R^{n-2} (GX.ConicalSpace, ℓ²), C_α ported from lean-causal, proper and geodesic, C_2π ≅ ℂ, apex not Euclidean for α ≠ 2π; its metric topology is the quotient topology of Γ_1\(D_inf × R^{n-2}) (GX.conicalMetricHomeo) and it is Euclidean along the developing map on {r>0} (GX.conical_locally_euclidean_prod).

l.350–351: the holonomy is offered by the paper only as 'an obstruction', and it is one only for α ∉ 2πN*: for α ∈ 2πN*, α ≠ 2π, the holonomy is trivial and does not obstruct, so the argument as written does not cover those angles. The claim itself is true there as well (the developing map is k-to-1 around the axis, so no chart covers it): GX.conical proves support = univ ↔ α = 2π, and the whole axis singular for α ≠ 2π. The metric side agrees: Cone.apex_not_euclidean for every α ≠ 2π (GX.conical_metric).
questions: Informational (no change of status): the Riemannian metric dz²+dr²+α r²dθ² is represented by the distance of the flat cone C_α × R^{n-2} (ℓ²; lean-causal kb/0021), not by mathlib's IsRiemannianManifold; 'locally Euclidean on {r>0}' is proved as a local isometry with the Euclidean distance through the developing map (GX.conical_locally_euclidean_prod).
notes_on_representation: 'cannot be extended to the whole R^n' is formalized as: the unique maximal a.e. atlas of E_α = Γ_1\(D_inf × Z) has support univ iff α = 2π (GX.conical); this is the paper's notion of the structure extending, not a reading.

The Riemannian metric is represented by its distance (flat cone C_α, ℓ²-product with R^{n-2}; DEC-47's cone angle α), the library having no Riemannian metrics; locally Euclidean along the developing map on {r>0} (GX.conical_locally_euclidean_prod).
